To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) students and the teacher negotiate the use of space in a university lecture room, and (2) they do so by means of social actions such as moving, pointing, and gesturing.

the participants (re)configure the space for participating in the class by using their bodies, objects, and the environment in various ways, such as moving around the room, sitting in a certain place, and using a white board.
the participants of a Finnish Sign Language (FinSL) class negotiate and reconfigure the lecture hall space to accommodate visual-embodied communication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the students, as a collective, negotiate the space in which they are situated and with how they orient themselves in relation to the space.
the question of how space is mediated in social interactions, and how it mediates the participants' interactions.
how the participants (re)configure the space for visual-embodied social interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the participants in the study are able to configure and reconfigure space for visual-embodied social interaction to a certain extent, but the architectural specifications of the space restrict the possibilities.
the space is not only a physical entity but also a social construct, a normative actor, and a mediator in interaction.

the students and the teacher orient to the architectural specifications of the lecture hall in their social actions, and they also negotiate the space to suit visual-visual and visual-embodied social interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the space of the lecture hall, in this particular case, is configured through the social actions of the teacher and students as they negotiate their ways into and through the space.
the students and teacher are engaged in a process of (re)configuring space in order to facilitate their participation in a sign language class.

the participants' social actions in a lecture hall are mediated by the architectural specifications and by their own embodied and linguistic actions, and that these social actions are not independent of one another.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the students' actions are not random or chaotic.
the students' and teacher's social actions are not just actions of a social nature, but also actions of a spatial nature.
the participants in a visual-embodied class configure and reconfigure space to suit the needs of the class.
